 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the claimant in O.P.(MV) No.92 of 2010 on the files of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kollam.
The respondents herein are the respondents before the Tribunal.

2. The case of the appellant/claimant is that on 12.09.2008, at 11.45 p.m., while the claimant was pillion riding on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-2/Y-5545 ridden by the second respondent, in a rash and negligent manner, ran into a heap of stones which was kept on the side of the road at Karikodu Junction and as a result of the accident, the appellant sustained serious injuries.

The appellant approached the Tribunal claiming a total compensation of 3,00,000/-.
3.
Before the Tribunal, the first, second and the third respondents are the owner, driver and the insurer of the offending vehicle respectively.
Though notice was issued to the respondents, the first and second respondents remained absent 2025:KER:40017 MACA NO. 1395 OF 2013 and were set ex parte.
Before the Tribunal, Exts.A1 to A10 documents were marked on the side of the appellant.
Pws.1 and 2 were examined.
No oral or documentary evidence were adduced on the side of the respondents.
The third respondent - insurer had a valid policy for KL-2/Y-5545 motorcycle.
The appellant had filed a private complaint before the Magistrate Court and it was forwarded to the police.
The police conducted an investigation and filed a refer report.
Though the appellant had filed a complaint, there is no allegation that he had sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle by the rider - the second respondent.
Aggrieved by the dismissal of the original petition before the Tribunal, the appellant has come up with this appeal.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent insurer.
5.

The learned counsel for the appellant submits that the vehicle was having valid insurance policy and the claimant 2025:KER:40017 MACA NO. 1395 OF 2013 was a pillion rider and due to the rashness and negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, the appellant sustained injuries.
Hence, he was entitled for compensation for the injuries sustained in the accident.
6. The learned standing counsel appearing for the respondent - insurer submitted that the appellant has not alleged negligence against the rider of the motorcycle.
The fact that the claimant was a pillion rider is admitted.

However without alleging and proving negligence on the part of the second respondent, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay any compensation to the appellant Rajesh Joy@Joby vs Sreekantan Pillai on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40091617/
2 for the injuries sustained.
7. I have considered the rival contentions.
8. The accident occurred while the claimant was pillion riding on the motorcycle.

In the claim petition as well as before the Tribunal, the claimant did not have a case that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, who is the second respondent.

The claimant 2025:KER:40017 MACA NO. 1395 OF 2013 alleged that the motorcycle ran into a heap of stones, which was kept on the side of the road, due to the flashing of the headlight of another vehicle which came in the opposite direction.

While he was examined as PW1, he deposed before the Tribunal that the accident occurred only due to the negligence of the driver of the vehicle, which came in the opposite direction and further deposed that there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
It is the bounden duty of the claimant to prove negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle to claim compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act.
The owner, rider and the insurer of the motorcycle were arrayed as the respondents in the case.
Unless the claimant proves and succeeds in establishing that there was negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, he cannot claim compensation for the injuries sustained.
9. The learned counsel for the appellant also sought to consider the claim under Section 163 A of the Motor Vehicles act.

The Tribunal has found that since the annual income 2025:KER:40017 MACA NO. 1395 OF 2013 claimed by the appellant exceeded Rs.40,000/-, the appellant is not entitled to get compensation under Section 163A of the Act.
Hence I find that the appellant/claimant is not entitled to raise claim under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The Tribunal has rightly found that since the claimant/appellant failed to prove negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, he is not entitled to get any compensation.
I do not find any reason to interfere with the said finding of the Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appeal stands dismissed.
